version 0.1.0; PROJECT spacetimes: Revision_Deflation: checks of the history of the model along the deflation clock (couplings that grow as exp(gsum x4))

column4: thresholds of the model, computed again: a pair of fermions is bound if D_VS > 1.67981; matter is self-bound if C > 3.7011 (3 pi^2/8 = 3.7011) or, with the negative-energy states, C > 5.9218 (3 pi^2/5 = 5.9218). On a deflating spacetime D_VS and C grow as exp(gsum x4), so each threshold is passed at a definite x4

along the clock, wherever the gap is below 0.05 E_F the critical temperature is 0.567 times the gap (largest deviation 0.0020); the gap of the vector channel is at every moment at least as large as the gap with the radial mode alone, and that at least as large as the gap of the two-form channel; the gap never decreases as the deflation proceeds (four sets of m_s/m and k_F/m, 34 moments each)

growth of the gap: for a weakly coupled state the gap is proportional to exp(-1/lambda), where lambda = lambda_S + lambda_P is the sum of the pairing strengths of the radial mode and of the phase mode in the vector channel, and lambda grows as exp(tau_d), which gives d ln(gap)/d tau_d = 1/lambda; in the computed histories lambda d ln(gap)/d tau_d lies between 1.00 and 1.03 wherever 1e-6 < gap/E_F < 0.02: the gap grows much faster than the couplings, by one e-folding in the time 1/(gsum/lambda)

the moment at which a pair becomes bound: just below D_c the scattering length is large and negative (-134.0/m_s at 0.99 D_c), just above large and positive (135.9/m_s at 1.01 D_c); the binding energy starts as a power of the distance from the threshold with the exponents 2.01 (between 2 and 4 per cent above D_c) and 2.01 (between 4 and 8 per cent), that is quadratically: E_b ~ (exp(tau_pair) - 1)^2 m_s^2/m. Because E_b vanishes at the threshold, the pair cannot follow the deflation adiabatically at first, however slow the deflation is

matter of fixed density loses the fermion mass (the Vorton-Scalar loses its expectation value in the matter) when C passes a critical value that falls with the density: k_F = 0.2 m: C = 151.892 (2.46 times pi^2 m^2/(4 k_F^2)); k_F = 0.5 m: C = 12.971 (1.31 times pi^2 m^2/(4 k_F^2)); k_F = 1 m: C = 2.556 (1.04 times pi^2 m^2/(4 k_F^2)); k_F = 2 m: C = 0.617 (1.00 times pi^2 m^2/(4 k_F^2)). The estimate C = pi^2 m^2/(4 k_F^2) of the main project is reached at high density, where the transition happens at weak coupling; at low density the critical C is larger. On a deflating spacetime every piece of matter becomes abnormal at a definite x4, the denser the earlier

the field beyond which the one-loop potential of the Vorton-Scalar lies below its vacuum value decreases monotonically as C grows: 24.7 v_VS at C = 1, 1.77 v_VS at C = 10. As the deflation proceeds the barrier that protects the vacuum moves in towards the vacuum value

the temperature T_half at which the fermions lose half of their mass, in units of the (constant) fermion mass, falls monotonically as g_VS grows, for m_s/m = 0.3, 1 and 3 (26 of the 30 moments examined; it is of the order of the four-dimensional vacuum value m/g_VS, which falls as exp(-gsum x4/2)): matter of a fixed temperature melts at a definite x4. No melting temperature can be given for m_s/m = 0.3 from g_VS = 1.69 (C = 32) on; there the Hartree potential ceases to exist at 1.05 v_VS before the expectation value has fallen, because the one-loop potential turns over too close to the vacuum value

order of events: the pair of fermions becomes bound before the one-loop potential of the Vorton-Scalar has fallen below its vacuum value at a field of 3 v_VS only for the mass ratios m_s/m = 10, 30 of the six ratios 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30 examined (the condition is 4 pi D_c m/m_s < 4.27, i.e. m_s/m > 4.9): for a light radial mode the deflation destabilizes the vacuum first
